articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino leaving USMNT for Manchester United just months after signing new deal
articles.summary: The Argentine coach will lead the Americans against Haiti before taking over a struggling Premier League giant, leaving U.S. Soccer searching for a replaceme...
articles.body:
FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. — Barely 100 days into his second term as U.S. coach, Mauricio Pochettino is leaving.

Barring a last-minute snag, his expected move to Manchester United will become official Friday, Yahoo Sports has learned.

An expected midday announcement in England — and early morning in the U.S. — will end a whirling week of speculation and multiparty negotiations that unfolded not so quietly while he continued overseeing U.S. preparations at the national training center near Atlanta.

Sources said Pochettino, 54, will complete his two-year tenure with the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals against Haiti — Saturday in Miami and Tuesday in Cincinnati — before taking charge of a storied Premier League club off to its worst start in 40 years.

U.S. Soccer officials have not commented on the situation all week.

Pochettino is scheduled to address the media early Friday, a common practice the day before a game.

Pochettino will return to his coaching roots on the European club circuit, where he worked for Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, among others, before dipping his toes into international waters for the first time with the U.S.

Pochettino had spoken with United on three separate occasions over the years but never received the luminous job. He is expected to debut Nov. 22 at Liverpool.

His U.S. finale will mark the end of a 37-match spell featuring a World Cup campaign that galvanized the nation for several weeks over the summer before a humbling, Round-of-16 defeat to Belgium.

The breakup comes a little more than three months after he and the U.S. Soccer Federation renewed their partnership with the expectation he would guide the team for four years and reach new heights at the 2030 World Cup.

But rehiring a coach with strong ties to the European scene — aside from the jobs, he has kept homes in London and Barcelona and never lived in the U.S. — came with the risk of him departing early. Even during the yearlong run-up to this year's 2026 World Cup, Pochettino was reportedly on Tottenham and AC Milan's short list.

The USSF is expected to begin its search for a replacement immediately.

Potential candidates include Nashville SC's B.J. Callaghan, an assistant on Gregg Berhalter's 2022 World Cup squad and later the interim head coach; former Belgium and Portugal boss Roberto Martinez; U.S. under-23 coach Steve Cherundolo, who was hired over the summer to prepare the 2028 Olympic team; and Pelegrino Matarazzo, a New Jersey native with extensive European credentials who is now in charge of Spain's Real Sociedad.

Pep Guardiola — the famed former coach of Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City — would be on any team's list, though he seems much more likely to land in another European job and would probably demand a salary that dwarfed Pochettino's U.S.-record $6 million.

The USSF is not in any rush. Aside from having an opening just months into a nascent World Cup cycle, the U.S. will not play again with the full squad until late March. The next major tournament is the CONCACAF Gold Cup next summer. World Cup qualifying will begin no earlier than next fall.

The pathway to Pochettino's departure began Monday with reports out of England that he had emerged as United's top choice to succeed Michael Carrick, who was on the hot seat after just 10 months at the helm.

In subsequent days, United engaged in talks with Pochettino's representatives and the USSF, which had included a $10 million release clause in the contract the sides signed after the World Cup.

Carrick was fired Thursday, clearing the way for United to complete terms with Pochettino and finalize the USSF's fee.

After signing his new USSF deal in August, Pochettino set out to shape the next four years by introducing a dozen young players for a sweep of four home friendlies in the September-October window — a sign he was very much in it for the long run.

However, hours after opening camp Monday ahead of the Nations League quarterfinals, his long-term plans with the U.S. turned to quickly completing the United move.

articles.title: USA soccer sends emotional letter to players about pulling out of U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid Iran war
articles.summary: U.S. Soccer's letter to U-17 players reveals the emotional toll behind the Qatar World Cup withdrawal, citing the Level 3 travel advisory for Qatar.
articles.body: U.S. Soccer expressed its "shared disappointment" in a letter to players explaining its withdrawal from the upcoming U-17 World Cup in Qatar amid safety concerns surrounding the Iran war. The letter, obtained by Fox News Digital, praised the players and coaches for their preparation while explaining why the federation was canceling both its pre-tournament camp and participation in the competition. "We are writing to inform you of the difficult decision to cancel our World Cup pre-camp and our planned participation in the World Cup. We are extremely proud of the preparation by our players and coaches to represent the US in the World Cup," the letter said. TEAM USA WITHDRAWS FROM FIFA U-17 WORLD CUP AMID STATE DEPARTMENT TRAVEL WARNING IN MIDDLE EAST "Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances including the US State Department’s Level 3 Travel Advisory for Qatar and related directives for Embassy staff and families, we are no longer able to participate in the tournament. The well-being of our players and staff will always be our top priority." The withdrawal became public Wednesday, eight days before the tournament’s scheduled Nov. 19 start. The letter also instructed players to hold off on publicly discussing the decision until FIFA announced it, while telling them their clubs would receive official notification. "We will communicate this officially to your clubs today as well. We ask that you refrain from sharing this information or commenting publicly until such time that it has been communicated publicly by FIFA," the letter said. "Again, please accept our deepest appreciation for your commitment to US Soccer and our shared disappointment about these circumstances." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER The State Department’s Oct. 23 advisory urges Americans to reconsider travel to Qatar because of the risk of armed conflict. U.S. government employees must obtain special authorization to travel there. The advisory cites attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces against civilian airports and other infrastructure in neighboring Saudi Arabia, warning that the hostilities could spread rapidly beyond the immediate area. It also identifies risks to civilian aviation from regional political and military tensions. Americans who travel to Qatar are urged to prepare to shelter in place and have an emergency departure plan that does not depend on U.S. government assistance. Fox News Digital previously reported that an Iranian missile struck Qatar’s Al-Udeid Air Base in March. Qatari officials reported no injuries. Fox News Digital also reported that nonemergency U.S. government employees and their families were ordered out of Saudi Arabia on Oct. 23 over safety concerns. For the American players, the withdrawal ends a World Cup opportunity less than a week after head coach Alex Aldaz announced his 21-player roster Nov. 6. The Americans were scheduled to open against Montenegro on Nov. 21, face Chile on Nov. 24 and finish Group J play against Algeria on Nov. 27. The roster included Philadelphia Union forward Malik Jakupovic, who scored eight goals during qualifying, and players affiliated with European clubs including AC Milan, Ajax and PSV. The United States earned its place in February, winning its qualifying group in St. Vincent and the Grenadines. The Americans beat the hosts 8-0 and St. Kitts and Nevis 10-0 before clinching qualification with a 1-1 draw against the Dominican Republic. Nine members of that qualifying squad were included on the World Cup roster. This year’s competition is the second under the tournament’s expanded annual, 48-team format and the second of five consecutive editions awarded to Qatar. articles.title: Kamario Taylor drops ‘never a doubt’ truth bomb on Mississippi State return
articles.summary: Mississippi State football received a massive boost in re-adding quarterback Kamario Taylor for 2027. Taylor’s new collegiate contract prevents a College Fo...
articles.body:
Mississippi State football received a massive boost in re-adding quarterback Kamario Taylor for 2027 . Taylor's new collegiate contract prevents a College Football Transfer Portal entry. Now the dual-threat broke his silence on coming back to the Bulldogs.

Taylor addressed his decision to ESPN's Sportscenter on Thursday following agreeing to his $7.5 million deal.

"The decision was already made in all honesty. There was never a doubt in my mind, there was never even options for me to leave here," Taylor shared to Sportscenter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Taylor's decision comes amid Mississippi State's five-game losing streak and him losing the rest of his 2026 campaign. Taylor left the Oklahoma game early and never returned . So his 2027 return hands Bulldog fans something to cheer for during this slide.

Furthermore, Taylor's return likely will attract more wide receivers and other skill position recruits. Now coach Jeff Lebby and his staff can paint the picture of how future Bulldogs can work with the dynamic passer and runner.

Taylor elevated the Bulldogs to a 4-0 start that included beating South Carolina 41-34, which was unranked at the time. Now that same Gamecocks team rose to No. 17 overall in the College Football Playoff poll released on Tuesday. Which makes the Bulldogs' win over them a high quality one.

Despite the 4-5 mark, Mississippi State can still clinch a bowl spot with two more victories. It starts with facing Auburn at Starksville on Saturday, with the Tigers coming in at 5-4 overall under first-year coach Alex Golesh. Tennessee Tech follows next in a non-conference showdown for the Bulldogs. All before ending the season against Ole Miss, which owns three regular season losses.

articles.title: What Northwestern coach David Braun said about Ohio State before game
articles.summary: Northwestern football head coach David Braun met with the media this week to preview Ohio State. Here's everything he said about the Buckeyes.
articles.body:
If Ohio State has any designs on keeping its Big Ten title and College Football Playoff hopes on life support, it has to beat Northwestern at home Saturday. The Buckeyes have lost two games in a row for the first time since 2011, and nobody is giving them a chance to do anything other than finish out the season and turn the page to next year.

But don't tell Northwestern head coach David Braun that. He met with the local media early this week to preview his team's travel to Columbus to take on the Scarlet and Gray, and he wasn't buying the fact that Ohio State won't be a significant challenge for his ball club.

Each week, we like to bring you what the opposing coach says about Ohio State before the game, and Braun was another very complimentary one who discussed the respect he had for head coach Ryan Day , the personnel on the team, and specifically Jeremiah Smith . The reporters also touched on the link between Northwestern offensive coordinator Chip Kelly and Day.

Ohio State and Northwestern are all set to kick off at Noon ET on Fox as a part of the Big Noon Game of the Week. We'll have it all for you before, during, and after the game.

articles.title: Megan Rapinoe, Julie Ertz and Jozy Altidore voted into the National Soccer Hall of Fame
articles.summary: national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday. David Beckham,...
articles.body:
Former U.S. national team standouts Megan Rapinoe, Jozy Altidore and Julie Ertz were among those elected to the National Soccer Hall of Fame on Thursday.

David Beckham, who helped grow soccer in the United States when he joined the LA Galaxy in 2007 and later as an owner of Inter Miami, was also voted into the Hall of Fame on the veteran ballot.

The group announced Thursday will be inducted on April 16 at the National Soccer Hall of Fame in Plano, Texas.

Rapinoe won a pair of Women's World Cup championships, an Olympic gold medal and the 2019 Ballon d'Or during her career. She was also honored with the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the nation's highest civilian honor, in 2022.

She retired from the national team in 2023 with 63 goals and 73 assists in 203 appearances. She also played for the Seattle Reign in the National Women's Soccer League from the league's first year in 2013 until her retirement.

Rapinoe was elected on the Hall of Fame's player ballot in her first year of eligibility. Her family, friends, and a group of fans surprised her with announcement of her election upon her arrival off a flight at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport.

"To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my teammates and friends, recognized like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams. So, I definitely was a part of some some great teams, and yeah, it's very special," Rapinoe said in a video posted to social media .

Altidore played in the World Cup twice and scored 42 international goals, to rank third in U.S. history, in 115 appearances for the national team. He also scored the winning goal for Toronto FC in the 2017 MLS Cup championship.

Ertz was considered among the best defensive midfielders in the world before her retirement in 2023 . She played in three Women's World Cups and was named U.S. Soccer's Player of the Year twice. She also played professionally for the NWSL's Chicago Red Stars from 2014 to 2021, before a short stint with Angel City in 2023.

Known for winning six Premier League titles while with Manchester United, Beckham looms large in the game's growth in the United States. He won back-to-back titles with the Galaxy, scoring 18 goals in 98 appearances. He exercised his option to buy an MLS expansion team in 2014, and Inter Miami joined the league in 2020.

Tatu, a Brazillian forward who scored 857 regular-season goals over a 21-year indoor soccer career, was also elected to the Hall of Fame on the veteran ballot. He is just the third indoor player to receive the honor.

Former U.S. national team coach Lothar Osiander was elected to the Hall of Fame on the builder ballot. Osiander coached the senior national team from 1986-88 and the under-23 team from 1988-92. He also had stints as head coach of the then-San Jose Clash and the LA Galaxy.

articles.title: Sydney Swans players will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
articles.summary: Four players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
articles.body:
Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said.

After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement.

Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August.

The men previously denied wrongdoing but apologised for breaching club standards by inviting women back to the hotel after a game and drinking.

Australian media reported that three women, understood to be adult entertainers, had alleged inappropriate touching during the incident at the Pullman Hotel and are reportedly looking into civil action.

"Due to the ongoing civil matter, Victoria Police is unable to make further comment," police said in a statement on Friday.

A fifth player, Riley Bice, who was also suspended by the club, had already been cleared by police.

Heeney welcomed the police announcement, saying the past three months had been "incredibly difficult for my family, [my fiancee] Steffie and those close to me".

"To my family and friends, your love and loyalty has meant more than words can do justice," he continued.
